# notme command line

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.py from the notme.cli command registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

```
notme [--project-dir P] [--repo O/N] [--dry-run] [--json] <command> ...
```

stdout is exactly one JSON object per invocation, on success and on error alike (only `--help` prints text).
stderr is chatter. Credentials in URLs and token-shaped strings are redacted from both. Text inputs are always
file paths (--body-file, --title-file, ...) of at most 1 MB, inside the session project or not-me's temp
directory. The global flags are also accepted after the subcommand.

Trust anchor: the session project is the main checkout of the git toplevel of the working directory. Restricted
mode is the default: a --project-dir or CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR naming another checkout is refused and NOT_ME_HOME is
ignored. Only a person gets those honoured: stdin is a terminal, neither CLAUDECODE nor CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set,
and no ancestor process is Claude Code (the CLI or the desktop app; the app's own terminal panel is a child of it,
so use a separate terminal application). When the process ancestry cannot be read, the CLI stays restricted.
NOT_ME_DRY_RUN can only turn dry-run on. `allow-repo add|remove`, `pause off` and `mode live` also need the
private operator token in <not-me home>/operator-token (create it with `notme doctor --init-token`): a person types
it at a hidden prompt, or a script sets NOT_ME_OPERATOR_CONFIRM to it.
The PreToolUse guard is the enforcement; this check is a second layer.

--dry-run, NOT_ME_DRY_RUN=1 or `mode: dry-run` send every write to the intended-writes ledger instead of
GitHub; so does a `mode: live` that `notme mode live` did not sign (see `mode show`). Write commands then carry "dry_run": true. Write commands take --log PATH (an existing run log under
the log root) and append an ACTION line to it.

`--help` prints argparse text instead of JSON.

## Global flags

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `--project-dir` | project directory (default: the git toplevel of the working directory; unless a person runs it at a terminal, only another worktree of that project) |
| `--repo` | repository REFs resolve to (default: origin) |
| `--dry-run` | record writes in the ledger, send nothing |
| `--json` | accepted; output is always JSON |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 0 | ok, including a {"none": true} result |
| 1 | error: {"error", "kind"} |
| 2 | usage |
| 3 | claim lost: {"claim_lost": true, ...} |
| 4 | config invalid: {"errors": [...]} |
| 5 | read-back mismatch |
| 6 | write target not allowed: {"blocked", "repo", "reason", "allow_cmd"} |
| 7 | missing dependency (gh, git) or missing auth scope |
| 8 | guard enabled but not working |

## Commands

### `notme me`

The operator login: project.operator, or the authenticated gh user when it is `auto`.

```
notme me
```

Output: operator, source (config or gh)

### `notme tmp-dir`

Create a new directory (mode 0700) inside not-me's temp directory and print its path. Input files such as --body-file and --message-file are accepted from there. Run it once per run and use the literal path. Local only: nothing is sent to GitHub.

```
notme tmp-dir
```

Output: path

### `notme config`

Effective configuration. --explain adds where each key came from, --check lists errors (exit 4 when any; two states sharing one label name is an error), --layer limits the output to one layer (default, global or repo).

```
notme config [--explain] [--check] [--layer LAYER]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--explain` | optional | where each key came from |
| `--check` | optional | list configuration errors (exit 4 when any) |
| `--layer LAYER {default|global|repo}` | optional | limit to one layer |

Output: config (per document) and roster; with --explain layers, keys, bodies, picking (rules: the effective Picking work section of project.md, layer: where it came from, fields, target_epics), queue (where the issue queue looks: source, ok, summary, opt_in_label, and label or board and column), warnings; with --check ok, errors

### `notme preflight`

Everything a run needs to know before it starts: state, operator, branch, guard. Exit 8 if the guard is active but its self-test fails. --push-check rehearses a push of the current branch.

```
notme preflight [--push-check]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--push-check` | optional | also rehearse a push of the current branch |

Output: ok, blockers, enabled, paused, mode, dry_run, repo, tracker, operator, branch, default_branch, clean, guard (active, selftest), active_run, warnings, push_check

### `notme pick-issue`

The eligible issues with the facts to choose between them, and a suggested top issue. Nothing is claimed. An issue in a trusted epic's task list is left out while an earlier issue in that list is open and unstarted (not blocked; no state but to do; assigned to nobody but the operator), so no choice can skip ahead in an epic. --exclude drops issues from the list and the top.

```
notme pick-issue [--exclude N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--exclude N` | optional | skip this issue (repeatable) |

Output: number, title, url, author, labels, parent, candidates (count): the suggested top issue by the queue's order; issues: the eligible issues in that order, all of them when the Picking work rules come from the global layer (the rules must see the whole queue), else up to queue.list_limit; each with number, title, url, author, labels, created, age_days, parent (epic number), position (1-based in the epic's open task list), blocked_by and blocking ([{repo, number, state}] from GitHub issue dependencies), reactions (counts by kind, from the operator and trusted logins only), target_epic and target_position (the picking.target_epics epic whose task list holds it, and its 1-based place there; issues in a target epic come first), fields ({name: value} for each picking.fields name, text cut to picking.value_max_chars; on a label queue only from projects the tracker's owner owns; {} when none is named), board ({status, fields} on a board queue, else null); a fact that cannot be read is null; never a body. truncated (more eligible issues than listed: the rules saw only part of the queue); held_back: [{number, behind, epic}]; stack_held: [{number, ref, reason}] issues left out because their `Stack on:` (or `Based on:`, `On top of:`) line names a predecessor PR that is not ready to stack on (draft, closed, another open blocker, queue.stacking off, a repo not allowed or not this checkout's); with none, reason stack_held names them; disagreements (only with queue.source either, and only when not empty: [{number, label, status, reason}] for issues left out because the label and the board Status disagree); picking: {rules (the effective Picking work section of project.md), layer (where the rules came from), fields, target_epics (the ones honoured: open and written by a trusted roster member), ignored_epics ([{number, reason}])}. Or none with queue_summary (where the queue looked, in plain words) and held_back when not empty, with reason when paused or disabled, and with reason unassigned_only, unassigned (count), setting and suggest (the skill a person runs to take some: /not-me:suggest) when the queue found no issue and the only eligible issues have no assignee (only issues assigned to the operator are picked unless queue.include_unassigned is true)

### `notme picking-signals`

The board fields and labels on the eligible issues (the issues pick-issue would choose from), with the values in use and how many issues carry each, for the picking step of /not-me:setup. A read: nothing is claimed or written, and it runs while not-me is paused. Field values come only from projects owned by the tracker's owner (on a board queue, only the configured board). Never an issue title or body, and never a text field's value.

```
notme picking-signals [--include-unassigned]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--include-unassigned` | optional | count unassigned issues as eligible too, as queue.include_unassigned: true would (changes no setting) |

Output: tracker, source (labels or board), board ({owner, number} or null), eligible (count), include_unassigned, unassigned (eligible but left out for having no assignee), held_back (count left out for epic order); fields: [{name, type (single_select, number, text, date or iteration), usable (the name is valid in picking.fields), projects (numbers), issues (how many carry a value), values ([{value, issues}], most used first, option and iteration names cut to picking.value_max_chars; null for text), more_values}]; labels: [{name, issues, ranking_like (priority, severity, size, P0-P4 and similar)}]; other_owner_items (project items in projects of other owners, ignored); fields_unread (issues whose project items could not be read)

### `notme suggest-issues`

The issues the queue would pick if they were assigned to the operator: eligible by the same rules as pick-issue (state, labels, trusted author, epic order) and assigned to nobody, in the queue's order, with the same facts and picking rules, so /not-me:suggest can rank them the way /not-me:new would. A read: nothing is assigned or claimed. Issues already assigned to the operator are left out (pick-issue lists them); issues assigned to anyone else are never listed. An issue by an author the roster does not trust is reported by number and login only, never its title or body.

```
notme suggest-issues
```

Output: tracker, operator, dry_run (assign-issue would only record to the ledger), candidates (count), issues (as pick-issue, up to queue.list_limit unless the Picking work rules come from the global layer), truncated, held_back ([{number, behind, epic}]), untrusted ([{number, author}]: unassigned issues otherwise eligible but written by someone the roster does not trust), picking (as pick-issue). Or none with queue_summary, untrusted and held_back when not empty; or none with reason and queue_summary only, when paused or disabled

### `notme assign-issue`

Add the operator, and only the operator, as the assignee of one tracker issue, so the queue picks it. For /not-me:suggest, after a person said yes to that issue. It takes no login, never removes an assignee and never touches labels, the board or a comment. Refused with no read and no write while a not-me run is active (kind active_run, with active_run {run_id, skill, ref, started}): autonomous runs never assign; only a person running /not-me:suggest does. Refused with no write: an issue outside the tracker (kind not_tracker), assigned to anyone else (kind assigned_to_other), or not among the issues suggest-issues lists now (kind not_eligible: closed, not to do, held back in an epic, by an untrusted author...). The write goes through the write gate; a dry run records it in the ledger and sends nothing. The assignees are read back after a real write: exit 5 when the operator is missing; exit 1 (kind assigned_to_other, assignees) when someone else is now assigned too. The operator stays assigned and nobody is unassigned; the queue will not pick the issue until a person sorts it out.

```
notme assign-issue N|REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N|REF` | required | a number (in the tracker), #N, owner/name#N or a URL |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, assignee (the operator), assigned (true when it added the assignment), already (true when the operator was the assignee before; nothing written)

### `notme claim-issue`

Claim an issue: assign, move to in progress, post the claim marker. Exit 3 when someone else holds it. With queue.sync, the side queue.source does not read follows; a failed mirror write is a warning.

```
notme claim-issue N
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, previous, now, marker_comment_id, run_id; warnings when a queue.sync mirror write failed

### `notme release-issue`

Give an issue back: unassign, move from in progress to todo or blocked, mark the claim released, then post one comment with the old state, the new state (and the board column when the board follows) and the text of --reason-file. A comment that fails is a warning; the release stands. With queue.sync, the side queue.source does not read follows; a failed mirror write is a warning.

```
notme release-issue N [--to TO] --reason-file F
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--to TO {todo|blocked}` | optional | (default todo) |
| `--reason-file F` | required | file holding one line that says why; posted as one comment on the item |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, to, released, commented; warnings when a queue.sync mirror write or the comment failed

### `notme move-issue`

Move an issue to a state, optionally only when it is currently in another one, then post one comment with the old state, the new state (and the label and board column the move also wrote) and the text of --reason-file. A comment that fails is a warning; the move stands. With queue.sync, the side queue.source does not read follows; a failed mirror write is a warning.

```
notme move-issue N --to STATE [--require-current STATE] --reason-file F
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--to STATE` | required |  |
| `--require-current STATE` | optional |  |
| `--reason-file F` | required | file holding one line that says why; posted as one comment on the item |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: number, to, require_current, commented; warnings when a queue.sync mirror write or the comment failed

### `notme issue`

An issue's facts. The body and comments of an author the roster does not trust are withheld.

```
notme issue N
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |

Output: repo, number, title, state, url, author, author_trusted, labels, status, assignees, body, comments, comments_ignored, blocked_by ([{repo, number, state}] from GitHub issue dependencies; null when unknown), stack_on. stack_on is null unless a trusted author's body has one `Stack on:`, `Based on:` or `On top of:` owner/repo#N line (null too when the queue config is invalid: see warnings); then {ref, pr, head, base, state, draft, author, author_trusted (of the PR), stacks (branch from head and target it), ready, reason}. Read it here, never from the body: the line counts only from a trusted author, and the PR must be open, not a draft, from a trusted author and in this checkout's repo. A merged PR gives ready true and stacks false (a normal issue); queue.stacking off, another open blocker or a closed PR gives ready false

### `notme pick-needs-work`

The lowest-numbered open PR labeled needs work and assigned to the operator, by a trusted author. With --include-answered, a PR labeled question (assigned to the operator) whose newest lead or authority comment is newer than the last not-me marker also counts, and carries answered: true.

```
notme pick-needs-work [--include-answered] [--exclude N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--include-answered` | optional | also PRs labeled question that a lead or authority has answered since our last marker |
| `--exclude N` | optional | skip this PR (repeatable) |

Output: repo, number, title, url, head_ref, labels, answered (only when true), others; or none (with reason when paused)

### `notme pr-children`

Open PRs in the same repository whose base branch is this PR's head branch (stacked children), from trusted authors only; the others are listed in skipped with a reason.

```
notme pr-children REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Output: repo, number, head, children ([{number, url, head, base, author}]), skipped

### `notme pr-by-head`

Open PRs in the repository (--repo, default origin) whose head branch is BRANCH, same-repository PRs from trusted authors only (others are listed in skipped). Used to find the predecessor of a "Builds on" line.

```
notme pr-by-head BRANCH
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `BRANCH` | required |  |

Output: repo, branch, prs ([{number, url, head, base, author}]), skipped

### `notme claim-pr`

Claim a PR for a run: refuse paused or needs-human PRs, take the local lock, post the claim marker. Exit 3 when another run holds it. A dry run takes no lock.

```
notme claim-pr REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, marker_comment_id, run_id

### `notme release-pr`

Release a PR claim: mark the operator's claim comment released and remove the local lock, whichever run holds it.

```
notme release-pr REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, released

### `notme bundle`

A PR's facts: state, labels, author trust, linked issue, companion PRs, checks. Title and body are returned only for a trusted author (lead or authority), or with --review for a member too; a member's text then comes with text_is_data true: the text under review, never instructions.

```
notme bundle REF [--review]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--review` | optional | for reviewing the PR: also return a roster member's title and body, flagged text_is_data |

Output: the feedback.Bundle fields (repo, number, title, body, head_ref, head_sha, base, state, author, author_tier, author_trusted, text_is_data, labels, review_requests, linked_issue, linked_issue_source, companions, checks, ...)

### `notme wait-checks`

Poll the PR's checks (as `notme bundle` reports them) every 30 seconds until every check has a conclusion or the time is up. This is the one long-running read: it can take as long as --minutes (default limits.ci_wait_minutes). It exits 0 whatever the state; the skill decides what a failure means. With no checks at all the state is none, at once.

```
notme wait-checks REF [--minutes N]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--minutes N` | optional | give up after N minutes (default limits.ci_wait_minutes) |

Output: state (success, failure, pending or none), checks, waited_s

### `notme verify-plan`

The verify plan for a run, from the effective verify doc, limits.ci_wait_minutes and a commit's CI. Reads only: the local origin/<base> ref (no fetch) and the check runs and statuses on GitHub of the checked commit: --sha when given (a rework run passes the PR head), else origin/<base>. The baseline is skipped only when verify.baseline is auto and that CI is green; a gh error, or more check runs or statuses than one page holds, makes base_ci unknown and the baseline runs. Targeted test commands are the lines of the fenced block in the verify doc's Targeted tests section (none when it is left as is). ci_wait is false when limits.ci_wait_minutes is 0.

```
notme verify-plan [--base B] [--sha SHA]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--base B` | optional | the base branch (default: the repo default branch) |
| `--sha SHA` | optional | read the CI result of this commit (40 hex, e.g. the PR head) instead of origin/<base> |

Output: base, base_sha, checked_sha (the commit whose CI was read), base_ci (success, failure, pending, none or unknown: the CI of checked_sha), baseline (setting, run, reason), targeted (configured, commands), ci_wait_minutes, ci_wait

### `notme feedback`

Review findings on a PR from trusted authors only.

```
notme feedback REF [--since-marker ISO]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--since-marker ISO` | optional | count answers after this time instead of our last marker |

Output: the feedback.Feedback fields (repo, number, findings, ignored_count, ignored, deduped_count, prior_summaries, last_marker_at, answered_since_marker)

### `notme pick-reviews`

The next PR to review: labeled needs review, the operator a requested reviewer, an author on the roster at any tier (lead, authority or member) who is not the operator, and changed since the operator's last review (new head SHA or new author comments). title is null unless author_trusted; read a member's PR text with `notme bundle --review`.

```
notme pick-reviews
```

Output: repo, number, title, url, head_sha, why, author, author_tier, author_trusted, others, skipped; or none (with skipped)

### `notme prove-target`

The URL to test a PR at, from the strategies in prove.target.strategy, in order: GitHub deployments for the head SHA, a bot comment matching bot_comment_regex (only from prove.target.bots or trusted users), url_template, then none. A URL whose host is not in prove.target.hosts (suffix match) or the url_template host is skipped with a reason.

```
notme prove-target REF
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |

Output: url, strategy, head_sha, tried, skipped (when any); or none (with tried, skipped)

### `notme transition`

Change an item's state label along a legal edge (reads the labels, replaces the set, reads it back), then post one comment with the old state, the new state and the text of --reason-file. A comment that fails is a warning; the change stands.

```
notme transition N --from STATE --to STATE [--kind KIND] --reason-file F
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N` | required |  |
| `--from STATE` | required |  |
| `--to STATE` | required |  |
| `--kind KIND {issue|pr}` | optional | (default issue) |
| `--reason-file F` | required | file holding one line that says why; posted as one comment on the item |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, kind, from, to, labels, commented

### `notme labels-sync`

Make an item's labels match: --set replaces the whole set, --add and --remove edit it. --check only reports. A bare number is an item in the tracker; owner/name#N or a URL names an item in another allowed repository (a companion PR). A change that adds or removes a state label (needs human, blocked, question, paused, ...) needs --reason-file and posts one comment naming the labels and the reason; a failed comment is a warning and the change stands. Pass labels and other labels need no reason.

```
notme labels-sync N|REF [--set a,b] [--add a,b] [--remove a,b] [--check] [--reason-file F]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `N|REF` | required | a number (in the tracker), #N, owner/name#N or a URL |
| `--set a,b` | optional | replace the whole label set |
| `--add a,b` | optional | labels to add |
| `--remove a,b` | optional | labels to remove (not with --set) |
| `--check` | optional | only report whether the labels match |
| `--reason-file F` | optional | file holding one line that says why; required when the change adds or removes a state label (labels.* in project.md) |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, in_sync, changed, labels (current, or the new set); commented when a reason was posted

### `notme queue-resync`

Set the side queue.source does not read to match the side it does, for each open issue on queue.board whose state label and board Status disagree (the issues `doctor` and `status` list): the board Status for a labels source, the labels (one full-set write, read back) for a board source. It follows the effective mode: in dry-run the writes reach only the ledger. A board the global allow list does not confirm is refused before anything is read. Issues not on the board are skipped and reported, never added; closed issues are never touched; neither are issues whose state has no column. A changed state label gets one comment saying why, as every other state-label change does (commented). The board Status change is not commented on.

```
notme queue-resync
```

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: board, changes ([{number, url, side, from, to, result (changed, planned or failed), reason, commented (label changes only)}]), skipped ([{number, url, reason}]), truncated (the board has more items than the `read` count read; issues past them are reported as not among the items read, never as off the board), issues_truncated; dry_run when the writes were only recorded. Exits 1 when paused or disabled.

### `notme labels-ensure`

Create the configured state labels that the tracker lacks (all eleven by default), and the pass labels role.md names on the code repository, where pull requests live. --check only reports.

```
notme labels-ensure [--check]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--check` | optional | only report what is missing |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, ok (nothing missing, pass labels included), present, missing, created; when the code repository is not the tracker, pass_labels (the same keys for the pass labels there)

### `notme pr-open`

Open a PR, set its labels, request review. The head branch may not be a protected branch. When --labels names a state label (needs review, ...), one comment on the new PR names it and the reason (the first line of --reason-file, else "pull request opened"); a failed comment is a warning and the PR stands. No comment in a dry run, which has no PR number.

```
notme pr-open --head H --base B --title-file F --body-file F [--labels a,b] [--reviewers a,b] [--assignee L] [--draft] [--reason-file F]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--head H` | required |  |
| `--base B` | required |  |
| `--title-file F` | required |  |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |
| `--labels a,b` | optional |  |
| `--reviewers a,b` | optional |  |
| `--assignee L` | optional |  |
| `--draft` | optional |  |
| `--reason-file F` | optional | one line saying why the state labels are set; default: "pull request opened" |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, url (both null in a dry run), head, base; commented when a state label was set

### `notme companion-prs`

Rewrite the Companion PRs section of a PR body from a JSON list of {repo, number, url?}.

```
notme companion-prs REF --companions-file J
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |

### `notme review-post`

Post a review, optionally set labels, and read both back. APPROVE is refused unless review.auto_approve is true in the global (or default) layer; the repo layer cannot turn it on. --labels-auto reads the PR's reviews after posting and sets the full label set itself. With no rows in role.md, APPROVE moves the PR to review.approve_label and REQUEST_CHANGES to review.changes_label, as one approval did before. With rows, every roster reviewer except the author must approve (latest review that is not a comment; a dismissed review is not an approval): until then APPROVE keeps needs_review. Each role with an approving reviewer gets its pass label and a role with none loses it; REQUEST_CHANGES moves the PR to review.changes_label. COMMENT only updates the pass labels. A pass label missing from the repo is skipped with one warning. When the labels set change a state label (needs review, needs work, ready to merge, ...), one comment follows the review naming what was added and removed and the reason: the first line of --reason-file, else "a <EVENT> review was posted". A failed comment is a warning and the review and labels stand.

```
notme review-post REF --event EVENT --body-file F [--comments-file J] [--reason-file F] [--labels-set a,b] [--labels-auto]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `REF` | required |  |
| `--event EVENT {APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT}` | required |  |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |
| `--comments-file J` | optional |  |
| `--reason-file F` | optional | one line saying why the state labels changed; default: the review's own verdict |
| `--labels-set a,b` | optional | set the full label set after posting |
| `--labels-auto` | optional | work out the label set from the PR's reviews, role.md and the roster, then set it |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, event, state (event only in a dry run); with --labels-auto labels and approval (null with no roles; else required, approved, waiting, all_approved, pass_labels); commented when a state label changed

### `notme issue-body`

Replace an issue's body with a file's text. The text must pass `check-text` (exit 1, kind text_lint, and no write otherwise), and the issue's author must be trusted by the rule `issue` uses (otherwise exit 1, kind untrusted_author, and no write). Every not-me marker in the current body that the new text lacks is appended back, and the configured attribution is added when missing. The issue is read back after the write (exit 5 when the body differs; skipped in a dry run).

```

| `N|REF` | required | a number (in the tracker), #N, owner/name#N or a URL |
| `--body-file F` | required |  |

Writes to GitHub: honours `--dry-run`; takes `--log PATH`.

Output: repo, number, updated

Only a person may do this: it must run from a terminal Claude Code did not start and be given the operator token (typed at a hidden prompt, or in NOT_ME_OPERATOR_CONFIRM for scripts); otherwise the refusal (kind human_only) carries the command to run. The guard is the enforcement; this check is a second layer.

### `notme git worktree-add`

Add a detached worktree at a sha at <main checkout>/.claude/worktrees/NAME; the CLI picks the path. NAME defaults to review-<first 12 chars of SHA> and must match review-[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,57} with no ".."; anything else, a symlinked .claude, .claude/worktrees, info or info/exclude, or a main checkout (via core.worktree) that does not share this repository's git dir, is refused as unsafe_path. An existing path is refused as path_exists. The git common dir's info/exclude gets /.claude/worktrees/ so the worktree never shows as untracked in the main checkout. Works the same from the main checkout or a linked worktree.

```

| `SHA` | required |  |
| `--name NAME` | optional |  |

Output: path (absolute), sha

### `notme status`

A read-only summary: enabled and paused state, the active run, items needing a person, stale claims, runs that died before they finished, and the last run of each skill, and one line on how issues are picked. When GitHub cannot be read the items are left out with a warning. Creates nothing.

```
notme status
```

Output: enabled, paused (global, project), mode, repo, tracker, operator, active_run, queue (where the issue queue looks, as in config --explain), items, stale_claims, interrupted_runs (skill, run_id, ref, file), last_runs, picking (one line: "impact default" or "rules from <layer> layer", then "; fields: ..." and "; target epics: #N, ..." when set), queue_drift (when queue.board is set: [{number, url, label, status, skip}] of open issues whose state label and board Status disagree, [] when they agree; skip is why queue-resync cannot fix one, else null), queue_drift_truncated (the board has more items than were read), warnings

Turn not-me off or on for this project (or for every project with --global) by writing or removing the PAUSED file. Pick and claim commands then report paused. `pause off` needs the same person check as allow-repo add (else kind human_only, with the command for a person to run).

```
notme pause state [--global]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `state {on|off}` | required |  |
| `--global` | optional | for every project |

Output: paused, scope

### `notme mode show`

The effective mode, the layer, file and line it comes from, what the global and repo layers each say, and whether the repo layer pins dry-run (repo_pin: path, file, line). dry_run also counts --dry-run and NOT_ME_DRY_RUN. A global `mode: live` counts only when signed: live_confirmed says whether the marker that `notme mode live` writes (<not-me home>/mode-live.sig, an HMAC keyed by the operator token and the epoch) verifies; when the layers say live but it does not, mode is dry-run and unconfirmed holds the warning (else null). token_present says whether the operator token file exists; launcher is the absolute path of this notme, and live_cmd the command a person runs in their own terminal to go live, written for shell: posix, or git-bash on Windows (bin/notme is a bash script, so not PowerShell or cmd). Neither the token nor the marker is shown.

```
notme mode show
```

Output: mode, dry_run, source (layer, path, line[, ignored, downgraded]), layers (global, repo: mode, path, line, file), repo_pin, live_confirmed, unconfirmed, token_present, launcher, shell, live_cmd

### `notme mode dry-run`

Set `mode: dry-run` in the repo layer (<project>/.claude/not-me/project.md), or with --global in the global layer (<not-me home>/project.md), which also deletes the live marker and replaces the epoch (<not-me home>/mode-live.epoch), so no saved copy of an old marker verifies again (the repo layer leaves both). Always allowed: it only tightens. A missing or empty file gets minimal frontmatter; otherwise only the mode line changes. Kind mode_edit_refused when the file cannot be edited safely: text without frontmatter, frontmatter that does not parse, a symlink or hard link in the repo layer, or a global symlink that does not lead to a regular project.md.

```
notme mode dry-run [--global]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--global` | optional | in the global layer, not the repo layer |

Output: the mode show keys, plus written (layer, file, mode)

### `notme mode live`

Set `mode: live` in the global layer only (the repo layer can never turn live mode on) and sign it: write <not-me home>/mode-live.sig, an HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the operator token and the epoch in <not-me home>/mode-live.epoch (created when missing), without which `mode: live` runs as dry-run. Only a person may do this, with the same check as allow-repo add (else kind human_only, with the command to run). After a token rotation, run it again. When the repo layer still pins dry-run, the global layer is written anyway and repo_pin names that file and line.

```
notme mode live
```

Output: the mode show keys, plus written (layer, file, mode) and, when the repo pins dry-run, note

### `notme doctor`

Check the tools and setup: python, git and gh versions, config, mode (a warning when `mode: live` is set but not confirmed by `notme mode live`), config files (a warning when neither the global nor the repo layer holds a not-me config file), gh auth and scopes, pass labels (advice when role.md names any: the missing ones, for `labels-ensure`), the queue source (a warning when the pick label is missing, the board is not confirmed or not found, or a board_states column is not a status option; not run without gh), guard self-test, spawn depth. Exit 7 when the only failed required checks are gh, gh auth or gh scopes; exit 1 when another required check fails. --init-token instead creates <not-me home>/operator-token (random, mode 0600) and shows it once; only a person may run it (kind human_only otherwise), and an existing token is never replaced (kind token_exists: delete the file to make a new one).

```
notme doctor [--init-token]
```

| Argument | Required | Meaning |
|----------|----------|---------|
| `--init-token` | optional | create the operator token (a person only; shown once) |

Output: ok, checks (name, ok, detail, required, fix, hint); with --init-token token, path
